correctness.rationale: The length-\(32\) base data are checked directly: the published local spaces of \(H^{1,1,1}\) give pair histogram \(5:3,6:3\) and triple histogram \(6:1,7:3\); a direct Carlet-Gray reconstruction of \(\bar H^{2,0,0}\) gives pair histogram \(5:2,7:4\) and triple histogram \(8:4\). Under Plotkin extension, sibling pairs add one dimension and cross-parent pairs preserve rank. For triples from three distinct parents, three block-evaluation functionals are independent because all take value \(1\) on the all-one kernel word, so the extra Plotkin pattern is already realized by a kernel word. For a \(2+1\) parent pattern the extra Plotkin vector adds exactly one dimension. This proves \(P_{C^+}(j)=b\mathbf1_{\{j=5\}}+4P_C(j)\) and \(T_{C^+}(j)=8T_C(j)+4P_C(j-1)\), from which the closed forms follow. The verifier independently checks base ranks, recurrences, closed forms, and binomial total counts.

value.rationale: The primary paper singles out the exceptional infinite pair because ordinary rank, kernel dimension, and one-block profile all coincide, then explicitly proposes the multi-block hierarchy as the natural next invariant. The new result determines the entire second-level histogram and the complete third level for every member of that pair, rather than only another maximum. The closed formulas reveal stable structural separation at level three, rank at most \(7\) versus rank-\(8\) triples, and turn an open-ended hierarchy question into an exact infinite-family calculation.
